items: How I read your three answers

Answer 1: a claim passes only if this turn tried the claimed thing and it failed. Answer 2: the first six phrases are flagged always; not done, I've stopped, next step are flagged only in unattended or bypass mode, since every reply ends with a next step. Answer 3: mid-build design choices are mine in those modes; the approval gate stays.
Tell me if a reading is wrong.

items.caption: Two readings, on answers 2 and 3, are my interpretation.

items: Matches straight and curly apostrophes, adds the six phrases, reads the permission mode, flags the stall phrases only in unattended or bypass sessions, and makes the check really block twice. Today the second block never happens, because the check returns at the retry.

items.caption: Step 1 touches the claim pattern and the block counter.

items: A claim passes only when a tool call named the claimed thing and its result shows failure. A turn that ran only ls or git ls-files is blocked. If no thing can be picked out of the claim, any failed tool result counts. That fallback is a known limit.

items.caption: A probe program alone no longer counts.

items: #590: never wait, docs, version, QA page

In unattended or bypass mode, a design decision is chosen, recorded and carried on. This adds one rule sentence, extends the no-questions hook to bypass mode, adds a check for replies that hand you a decision, and posts a QA page.
Nothing from you until the QA page.
